newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES says stake acquisition by Gazprom unlikely.
newsitem.headline: UES says stake acquisition by Gazprom unlikely.

text.p: Russia's State Committee on Anti-Monopoly Policy is unlikely to allow natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom 0#GAZP.RUO to acquire a 25.1 percent stake in national power company Unified Energy System (UES) 0#EESR.RUO, a senior UES official said on Thursday.
Alexander Lopatin, director of asset management at UES, told Reuters that UES's regional power utility subsidiaries owed Gazprom about 20 trillion roubles.
Earlier a Gazprom spokesman said Gazprom intended to acquire a 25.1 percent stake in RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES).
UES's total debts are about 50 trillion roubles.

UES operates Russia's national power grid, owns many power stations and holds large stakes in almost all the "energo" regional utilities, which supply the bulk of Russia's power. It controls about four fifths of generating capacity in all.
It is Russia's biggest company by sales and biggest employer. Gazprom, the world's biggest gas company, is Russia's second biggest company by sales and third biggest employer.

"Firstly the anti-monopoly committee will not allow this, or at least it would be declared invalid. Secondly if it wants to buy shares on the open market it would be too expensive," Lopatin said of the proposed acquisition.
A 25 percent-plus-one share stake in UES would give Gazprom seats on the board and enough votes to block changes in its charter.
Gazprom already controls an 8.5 percent stake in UES which was acquired in January by a consortium headed by Natsionalny Rezervny Bank, which is closely linked to Gazprom.
Share analysts said it was possible that UES group debts to Gazprom could be swapped for equity in UES.
